it's just a couple of loops with some randomizers attached. the part where we pretend that it's something other than random mishmash is the douchey part. This is the kind of thing you get when everyone around you is afraid to say "hey, that's a cute idea or whatever, but let's not be lazy fucks and actually bang out the soundscape a bit."

Yeah, alright. Loops are common in soundtracking / sound design for art installations, not because people are lazy, but out of practical necessity for the format. You can’t really bang out 18 days of non-repeating soundtrack in a reasonable time. And thought goes into the arrangement of the loops even if its somewhat “random”. I may be biased as I’ve dabbled in looping and sound art.

I guess I can take offence that the journalist thought this was noteworthy because it was done by Thom Yorke. You could walk into any installation in an art school and write the same article, but it wouldn’t be news.

i think that's where the limitation comes in creatively - if you're creating a sound for an art installation the creative challenge is finding something that can work in the background without being obnoxious. the inability to actually make something appropriate for the forum is why they basically decided to let a computer do it for them. That's what I'm knocking - this isn't art.
Hm. I must have missed the part where they let a computer do the work. Or is there a more detailed article elsewhere?

The "evolving" part is the clue. What mechanism do you think determines this? Here's what they did: they collected a handful of sound types that can be merged together, and they dumped a script that says "randomly apply these" and there ya go.

I’ve used tools like Processing, SuperCollider, and Pure Data to make generative music. It’s a lot more involved than dumping samples in a script.

It’s possible Thom Yorke picked a few loops on his iPad while jerking off and called it art, because we all love to hate him. But it’s also possible he did a tiny bit more work than that. I would prefer not to assume so much from so little information.
